disputed.question: (a) What do the SRV records for the plain and .global. hosts return, and what do their targets point to?
disputed.reason: The closing sentence goes beyond what was observed. The summary says "One shard maps to one node target" and report.json says "One SRV target matches one shard / one node". Only one cluster was observed, with shardCount 1 and HA Disabled, and it published one SRV target. That does not show whether SRV lists one target per shard, per node or per cluster. It should read: this one-shard, HA-disabled cluster publishes one SRV target. The rest of (a) matches raw.json, raw_run1.json and dns_extra.json: one SRV record per host, port 10260, the CNAME chains to 20.42.93.93, no AAAA, no TXT, and NOERROR/NODATA for A on both cluster hosts.

disputed.question: (d) Does PyMongo print a CosmosDB warning?
disputed.reason: "With default filters it prints twice for every mongodb+srv URI" was generalised from warn_probe.py, which builds one client in a fresh process each time. Under Python's default warning action a UserWarning prints once per (module, line number). The second warning is always attributed to pymongo/synchronous/mongo_client.py:1916, so a second SRV client in the same process would not print it again, and a client built again from the same caller line would print nothing. The in-process steps b1 and b7, which show two warnings for both forms, ran under simplefilter('always'). What was observed: two warnings for the first SRV client in a fresh process, and one for a non-SRV client. The source-code statements are verified in the venv: the '.cosmos.azure.com' suffix check in mongo_client_shared._detect_external_db, the two call sites (constructor seeds, which are the URI host, then _resolve_srv on the resolved nodes) and the INFO path when the 'pymongo.client' logger is enabled for INFO.

disputed.question: Are there host forms beyond the plain host and .global.?
disputed.reason: The documentation status is overstated. Step b13 calls .ro.global. 'undocumented', and report.json's answer says none of the forms appears 'in the sources DECISIONS topic 3 cites'. The test checked only the service-issued strings and the text of DECISIONS.md; it did no Learn search. The Data API forms <cluster>.data[.global].mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com are on the data-api Learn page, which DECISIONS topic 3 cites under 'Learn and reference fixes', so that clause is wrong for them. Two things are supported: no form appears in any service-issued connection string, and .ro.global. is not mentioned anywhere in findings/phase4. The DNS, TLS and SCRAM observations in this conclusion match the raw responses, and the purpose of .ro.global. is correctly marked as inferred.

extra_observations: Secrets: I scanned every file in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-julietai-claude/40f65f7c-640c-44c6-8eab-a8434709e1ff/scratchpad/managed-tests/m-hosts/, including __pycache__. The password does not appear in raw, quote or quote_plus form, the userinfo form from the URIs is absent, and no 8-character fragment of any of these appears. There are no e-mail addresses. The only GUID is the scratchpad session id in file paths. Every URI carries <password-masked> or the service's literal <user>:<password>. Nothing needed redacting.

Outside this test's directory: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-julietai-claude/40f65f7c-640c-44c6-8eab-a8434709e1ff/scratchpad/managed-tests/show.raw.json (parent folder, written before m-hosts) holds an unmasked e-mail address in systemData.createdBy and lastModifiedBy and the subscription id in 'id'. This review did not change it because it is outside the test's scope; the orchestrator should mask it.

Report accuracy: three report.json step readings hard-code TTLs from run 1 that contradict the run-2 responses they sit next to. a-plain-dnspython-srv says TTL 30, but its response shows ttl 6. a-plain-dig-srv-answer says 'authoritative TTL 30 s per dnspython', but dnspython gave 6 in run 2 and 30 only in run 1. a-plain-target-dig-a-chain says 'both with TTL 30 s', but the recorded CNAME TTL is 20. No recorded answer had the aa flag, so 'authoritative' was an inference. My own query to ns1-07.azure-dns.com (+norecurse, aa set, 2026-11-25T21:25Z) returned TTL 30 for both SRV names, so the conclusion's 30 s is correct.

'Cluster names have no privatelink record' (step a11 and the private-endpoint conclusion) rests on one query: ddb-samples-shared.global.privatelink returned NXDOMAIN. My read-only authoritative queries at 21:25Z also returned NXDOMAIN for ddb-samples-shared.privatelink.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com and ddb-samples-shared.ro.global.privatelink.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com. The statement holds, but those queries are not in the report. The test's 'records <node>, <node>.global, <node>.ro.global' corrects the DECISIONS topic 3 open item 2 best guess, which names <cluster> and <cluster>.global records.

'The certificate CN has no DNS record' (step a9) was backed only by an empty +noall +answer A result, which hides the status, plus a getaddrinfo failure. My authoritative query returns NXDOMAIN for ed484574ee80.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com, so the claim is right.

'No private endpoint' (step a6) and 'none exists' (private-endpoint conclusion) are not shown by any m-hosts step: c4's --query left out properties.privateEndpointConnections. The parent-folder show.raw.json does show privateEndpointConnections [] and should be cited.

Step b13 (report.json step 71) says the .ro.global. name 'does not make the connection read-only here'. That goes beyond the hello flags: by design, no write was tried through that name, so writability there is unverified. The conclusion's wording, 'reports isWritablePrimary true and readOnly false', is the accurate one.

Step b12 says 'Non-SRV connections work only through the SRV target node names', which b13 contradicts: the .ro.global. node name is not an SRV target and it worked. The (b, extra) conclusion lists all three node names correctly.

Missing caveat on 'a tool that cannot use mongodb+srv needs the SRV target node name': a non-SRV string pinned to a node name skips SRV, so it would not follow the .global. redirection after a replica promotion. Whether node names stay stable through scaling, HA or maintenance, and what seed list a multi-shard cluster needs, were not tested.

Step z2's 'the listDatabases filter option is honoured' has no positive control, such as a filter that matches an existing database. An empty list proves only that mt_hosts is gone, which is true whether or not the filter was applied.

In the summary, (c, implication) equates the CLI help's 'default connection string' with the Self entry. Neither the help nor the list output marks any entry as default. The match is inferred through GET properties.connectionString, which the REST docs describe as 'The default mongo connection string' and which returned the Self string.

Step d3 says gitVersion, modules and internal.documentdb_versions 'appear only in hello and isMaster'. gitVersion, modules and openssl appear in neither command; only internal.documentdb_versions is limited to hello and isMaster. The conclusion text states this correctly.

OSS comparison, checked against /Users/julietai/claude/azure-documentdb-agent-readiness/findings/phase4/engine-tests/local-gateway-parity/report.json. hello matches key by key (maxWireVersion 25 vs 21; documentdb_versions and kind differ; endpointName and operationTime are managed-only; all limits, msg, readOnly and saslSupportedMechs are the same). buildInfo has the same key set (8.0.0 vs 7.0.0). The any-database and cluster privilege lists are identical. The 'different' verdicts for b4 and d9 reflect different provisioned users (managed root vs OSS readWriteAnyDatabase plus clusterAdmin), not one role behaving differently. Every comparison is against OSS 0.117, and ENGINE-TESTS.md says 0.117 results should be rerun on 1.2.0 before they are quoted, so endpointName, operationTime and the wire-version gap may be version effects rather than managed-only behaviour.

vs_open_source for b-plain-ping is 'not_tested_locally' in report.json but 'same' in the summary. 'same' is supportable because the OSS driver-floors test recorded a successful sync ping. The two should agree. OSS dropDatabase replies were never captured (the jsonschema test wrapper substitutes {ok: 1} when the call returns None), so not_tested_locally is right for b5 and z1.

New observation: on both managed and OSS 0.117, hello returns saslSupportedMechs ['SCRAM-SHA-256'] although the request was only {hello: 1} with no saslSupportedMechs user. MongoDB returns that field only when the request names a user.

endpointName echoes whichever node name the client connected to, including the .ro.global. name over a non-SRV connection, so it identifies the host name used rather than strictly the SRV form. All three names resolve to one IP, which suggests the value comes from SNI (inference).

The parent-folder show.raw.json reports dataApi.mode 'Disabled', yet both Data API host names resolve and are certificate SANs. Their DNS and certificate presence says nothing about whether the Data API is available, which was not tested.

Verified as reported: steps common to run 1 and run 2 differ only in run.py line numbers inside warning locations and in topology ids. The documentdb 1.0.0 CLI extension sends api-version 2026-06-01 (_list_connection_strings.py line 128). PyMongo's SRV parent-domain check and its handling of TXT NoAnswer as 'no options' match the source. DECISIONS topic 11 supports 2026-09-01 as the newest stable and 2026-10-15-preview as the newest preview version. DECISIONS topic 3 confirms that .global. had not been observed before and that the REST samples show one unnamed 'default connection string' entry.

Scope check: run.py writes only to mt_hosts (dropped at the end and confirmed gone). The admin commands are read-only. The az calls are help, list-connection-strings, show, replica list and the non-mutating POST listConnectionStrings. There are no configuration changes, and both runs finished in about 42 s.
summary: The m-hosts report is sound. Its main findings follow from the raw responses in raw.json, raw_run1.json and dns_extra.json. Each host form has one SRV target, which reaches 20.42.93.93 through a privatelink CNAME, and neither has TXT records. The cluster hosts have no A record, so non-SRV strings work only with node names. The .global. form resolves and authenticates on this single cluster with no replica. list-connection-strings returns GlobalReadWrite first and Self second, and GET returns the Self string. The hello, buildInfo, getParameter and getCmdLineOpts results are as stated, and so are the certificate SANs. I checked the OSS comparisons against local-gateway-parity/report.json: hello and buildInfo differ exactly as described, and the two privilege lists the services share are identical. Three conclusions go too far: (a) 'one shard maps to one node target' rests on a single one-shard cluster; the PyMongo warning 'prints twice for every mongodb+srv URI' rests on one client per process, and Python prints a warning only once per code location; and the extra-host-forms conclusion overstates documentation status ('undocumented', and the Data API forms do appear in a source DECISIONS cites). Smaller problems are listed in extra_observations: three step readings quote TTLs that contradict their own recorded run-2 responses, the 'no private endpoint' claim cites no step from this test, the listDatabases filter has no positive control, and one step reading says writes work through .ro.global. without a write test. Read-only authoritative DNS queries confirmed the TTL of 30 s, that the plain and .ro.global. cluster names have no privatelink record, and that the certificate CN returns NXDOMAIN. The test directory holds no password and no e-mail address, so nothing was redacted. The parent folder's show.raw.json does hold an unmasked e-mail address and the subscription id and needs masking by the orchestrator.
